messages:
maria: quick FYI — ran a focused probe on token-level attribution this morning. noticed TTFT jumps for long-context chat when kernel selector flips from microkernel-X to microkernel-Y and KV cache miss rate climbs ~3x. attaching a tiny log snippet below.

aj: can you paste the exact query shape and example config you ran?

maria: sure. run was on canary traffic + the new batcher heuristics (aggressive coalesce). config snippet: ```
batcher.window_ms=8
batcher.max_tokens=1024
kernel.selector.preference=latency_then_cost
kv.prefetch.enabled=true
```

devon: interesting — aggressive coalesce usually reduces per-token cost but can increase TTFT if it delays small urgent requests. were these mostly short responses or long generations?

maria: mostly long (200-600 tokens). but we also had a tail of short single-token responses that got queued.

samir: any kernel time breakdown? i.e., how much time spent in kernel exec vs kv lookup vs python orchestration?

maria: perf-bot sampled 1k traces. summary: ```
median TTFT: 72ms
90th TTFT: 230ms
median decode time (kernel): 39ms
90th decode time: 120ms
median kv lookup: 4ms
90th kv lookup: 45ms (spikes aligned with cache misses)
kernel switch overhead (estimate): +18ms tail
```

perf-bot: automated note — sampled traces collected at 2026-03-17T08:12Z. tagging traces with kernel_variant and kv_hit boolean.

aj: kernel switch overhead +18ms — that's large. is that from reinitializing CUDA kernels or from extra memcpy/KV marshaling?

maria: early signs point to memcpy / context warmup when switching between microkernel-X (optimized 4-bit path) and microkernel-Y (FP16 path). also seen increased serialization time when KV miss triggers remote fetch.

devon: can you add a quick histogram tile to the perf dashboard showing TTFT conditioned on (kernel_variant, kv_hit) and microbatch size? would help isolate if batching heuristics are misrouting short requests into long batches.

maria: on it. planning two tiles: 1) TTFT distribution sliced by kernel_variant+kv_hit, 2) queue wait time vs microbatch size.

samir: +1. also add a derived metric: "kernel_switch_count_per_minute" per worker — if that correlates with spikes we might throttle selector churn.

aj: for immediate mitigation, can we pin the kernel selector to prefer microkernel-X for routes with <1s budget or force kv.prefetch.enabled=false for the canary?

maria: i ran a quick A/B: disabling kv.prefetch reduced TTFT 90th by ~40ms but increased avg cost by ~6% because more contiguous batches were smaller.

devon: tradeoffs as expected. let's do a short-term config: keep prefetch enabled but increase batcher.window_ms=12 for canary to reduce churn. that should let microkernel stay steady longer.

maria: will deploy canary change now. will post results in 10–15m.

perf-bot: deploy event — canary config applied to 5% of production at 2026-03-17T08:28Z.

maria: quick follow-up after 12m: 90th TTFT dropped from 230ms -> 190ms on canary, kernel_switch_count_per_minute down 63%. kv miss rate unchanged.

aj: promising. can you also capture per-route SLI mapping? some routes are latency-sensitive (chat-short) and others are throughput-first (batch-embed).

maria: added route tag in traces and updated alerting rule: if route!=throughput and 95th_TTFT>200ms for 5m, page eng-runtime.

samir: one more ask — let's add a small instrumentation change: include kernel_choice_reason in span metadata (e.g., reason=kv_hit, reason=batch_size, reason=latency_slo) so we can attribute switching to policy.

maria: agreed. filing a tiny PR for trace fields now. pinging @aj for review.

aj: reviewing. also want a short write-up for the ops runbook describing mitigation knobs: batcher.window_ms, kv.prefetch.enabled, kernel.selector.preference. keep it <200 words.

maria: draft done, pushing to #eng-runtime-docs after PR merges.

perf-bot: monitoring note — continue sampling for 1 hour at 1% traces. will summarize after sampling window.

maria: thanks all — leaving the canary running. will post the perf summary and the new dashboard links shortly. :thumbsup:
